approachQuestion.prompt:
Multiplicative Reliability Runs

Each entry in `factors` is a positive integer multiplier. Count non-empty contiguous segments whose product is strictly less than limit.

Limits and assumptions:
• 0 ≤ n ≤ 200000; 1 ≤ factors[i] ≤ 10^6; 1 ≤ limit ≤ 10^12.
• All temporary products formed by extending a segment already below limit fit in signed 64-bit integers. Integer multiplication and exact division take constant time.
• No zero or negative factor is allowed. Input is read-only.

Examples:
1. factors = [2,3,1], limit = 6 → 4: the three singletons and [3,1].
2. factors = [1,1], limit = 1 → 0.

Choose one approach.
constraints: All temporary products formed by extending a segment already below limit fit in signed 64-bit integers. Integer multiplication and exact division take constant time.
No zero or negative factor is allowed. Input is read-only.

options.text: Return zero if limit is one. Otherwise multiply the incoming factor into a running product, divide out leftmost factors while the product is at least limit, then add the number of remaining suffixes.
options.feedback: Positive integer factors never decrease a product when appended. Dividing removes exactly the outgoing factor, including ones, and all remaining suffixes qualify.

options.text: For each start multiply consecutive factors and count products below limit, stopping when the threshold is reached.
options.feedback: Products cannot later decrease, so the stopping rule is valid, but starts can repeatedly traverse long runs of ones.

options.text: Use the same moving product but remove factors only while product is greater than limit.
options.feedback: Equality is forbidden: factors [2,3], limit 6 must not count the pair.

options.text: Round each natural logarithm to the nearest integer, compare sums of those rounded values against the rounded logarithm of limit, and count those below.
options.feedback: Rounding loses the strict product boundary. For factors [2], limit 3 both rounded logarithms are 1, rejecting a valid segment.

feedback.reason: All factors are at least one, so removing a left factor cannot increase the product.
details: If limit equals one return zero. Otherwise initialize product=1 and left=0. Multiply each incoming factor, divide out factors while product ≥ limit, and add right-left+1. Use exact integer operations; do not take logarithms.

All factors are at least one, so removing a left factor cannot increase the product. Divide exactly while the strict threshold is violated. For limit=1 no positive product can qualify; logarithmic approximations would risk boundary errors.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only “Count suffixes using an exact product” as specified in the method reveal. Choose the tightest worst-case running-time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Use unit-cost random access and arithmetic on machine words large enough for every index and sum.
Input is read-only and excluded from auxiliary space. The scalar or index-pair output is excluded; no candidate segment is copied.
The implementation is iterative with a constant call stack. No hashing is used; fixed alphabet arrays, when present, are direct indexed.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Each factor is multiplied once and divided out at most once.
details: For limit > 1, after repair the product is below limit and every suffix also qualifies because all factors are at least one. Each factor is multiplied once and divided out at most once. Only scalar state is kept. The limit=1 branch correctly rejects every positive product.
“O(n²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: A factor is divided out at most once after being multiplied in; shrinking loops do not repeat work for every starting index.
“O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: The method uses exact product updates, not sorting or a logarithm array, so neither the log factor nor n-sized storage is present.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Product, left/right indices, and the numeric count are scalars; valid segments are counted, not stored.
